sections.html: Pyrrhulina spilota is one of the most attractive species of its genus. Males reach up to 7-8 cm.
Like most tetras they feed happily on any type of usual fish food, even dried food items.

Usually P. spilota behave like "regular" tetras and swim in the open water. They prefer the upper third of the water column, but can be found anywhere in the tank. They don't damage any plants.

When the breeding season comes, the males occupy territories, preferably around a plant with broad leaves; if this is not available, a stone or a root will also do. Possible tankmates have to take care not to come too close to the spawning site.
Males can be easily distinguished from females. Males have silvery scales in the first third of the body and a contrasting marked anal fin. Both features are missing in the smaller females.

The fish spawn on the substrate the male has chosen as its territory. Most tetras are egg scatterers that take no care of their spawn. In contrast, Pyrrhulina produce a fairly compact spawn that looks much like the spawn of a cichlid. The male alone takes care of the eggs, as in labyrinth fish, and does so very seriously. When the offspring hatch and leave the leaf, the male's job is done and it returns to the behaviour of a regular tetra.
